answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit jobs or vote on payments. Rewards accrue only to bonded identities that complete work verified by randomly assigned peers, while provable fraud burns the bond. Creating a thousand aliases therefore does not create free influence: the attacker must tie up capital for each one and risks losing it. A summit vote can still favor a reef of colluding agents, so random audits and bond sizes must make the expected loss exceed the gain; velvet wording alone proves nothing.
